title: Bruising, mouth ulcers and tiredness — focused assessment and safe immediate decisions

blocks.text: Bruising, mouth ulcers and tiredness — focused assessment and safe immediate decisions
AMaC MRCP PACES23 • R5-224 • Station 2 acute consultation • Skills A–G plus relevant assessment • 20 minutes • 14 October 2026 • Educational assessment, not official PACES marking
A 56-year-old has new easy bruising, painful mouth ulcers and marked fatigue with intermittent fever. Take a focused history, explain your differential and initiate a safe management plan.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
Hook: Possible acute leukaemia with marrow failure; severe aplastic anaemia and other marrow diseases are alternatives.
Trap: Major bleeding, unstable observations or suspected neutropenic sepsis needs emergency admission. Avoid routine reassurance based on a single nonspecific symptom or delay pending outpatient repeat bloods.

rows: “First I want to check how unwell you are.”
ABCDE and vital signs as indicated.
“May I ask about these symptoms and exposures?”
Ask about spontaneous bleeding, epistaxis, infections, fever, weight loss, medicines and family history. Check pallor, petechiae, oral ulcers, lymph nodes, hepatosplenomegaly and stability.
“There are several causes, including one requiring prompt treatment.”
Possible acute leukaemia with marrow failure; severe aplastic anaemia and other marrow diseases are alternatives.
“I will arrange urgent tests and care.”

Same-day FBC with differential and urgent blood film; clotting, renal function and appropriate baseline studies; contact haematology urgently for suspected blasts/cytopenias. If febrile/neutropenic, initiate neutropenic sepsis pathway and antibiotics immediately.

Discharges despite major bleeding or febrile neutropenia

Coordinates appropriate transfusion and empiric IV antibiotics if neutropenic sepsis suspected

Uses sensitive explanation and a clear escalation plan

blocks.text: Patient is worried and asks “Could this be serious?” Only disclose clinical information if elicited. Respond to calm explanations; ask whether hospital assessment is necessary. Do not introduce a diagnosis the candidate has not explored.

THINK: Possible acute leukaemia with marrow failure; severe aplastic anaemia and other marrow diseases are alternatives. SAY: explain uncertainty. DO: Same-day FBC with differential and urgent blood film; clotting, renal function and appropriate baseline studies; contact haematology urgently for suspected blasts/cytopenias. If febrile/neutropenic, initiate neutropenic sepsis pathway and antibiotics immediately. NUMBERS: PACES 20-minute encounter. TRAP: avoid premature reassurance. FINISH: Major bleeding, unstable observations or suspected neutropenic sepsis needs emergency admission. Avoid routine reassurance based on a single nonspecific symptom or delay pending outpatient repeat bloods.
